chunks.title: [CLO Master Express Lesson 17] 3D Hanfu Special Recorded Lesson: Hanfu 3D Modeling and Scene Construction Production Tutorial
chunks.content: ## Hanfu 3D Modeling and Scene Construction Overview This section covers the fundamental workflow and tools used in CLO Master Express for 3D Hanfu modeling, including posture adjustment, panel creation, arrangement techniques, and sewing methods. Key terminology includes A pose, T pose, X-Ren combination point, positioning ball tool, internal multidirectional tool, and sewing seam. ### Model Preparation and Posture Adjustment - Start with a character model (e.g., Kelly Jinlan). - Change the model’s posture from A pose to T pose using the X-Ren combination point to facilitate Hanfu arrangement. - This pose change ensures easier manipulation and fitting of garments. ### Hanfu Board Creation and Scaling - Since there is no direct Hanfu board, create one by drawing a Miao board on a straight board. - Enlarge the board to a 1:1 scale. - Use the 2D measurement tool to verify dimensions for accuracy. - Employ internal lifting and multidirectional tools for drawing the Hanfu board and its collar parts. - Use Ctrl key to draw curves; delete wrong lines as needed. ### Panel Drawing and Editing - Draw collar, embroidery, and embroidery details using the internal multidirectional tool. - Use the Edit Curve tool to refine panel shapes. - For breakpoints in panels, merge or convert them to free-range points before engraving. - After drawing, engrave panels individually ensuring no breakpoints interfere. ### Panel Arrangement and Sewing - Remove previous curved panels and copy symmetrical halves. - Use the positioning ball tool to arrange panels on the virtual model, rotating and adjusting angles as necessary. - For screen coordinate positioning, frequently rotate and check placement. - Sew simple seams under panels; rework unnecessary panels. - Simulate garment fit after arrangement and sewing. --- ## Collar and Butterfly Knot Construction This section focuses on detailed collar creation, butterfly knot modeling, and sewing techniques, emphasizing the use of the positioning ball and sewing tools. ### Collar Arrangement and Simulation - Arrange collar panels using the positioning ball tool. - Add internal lines and folds to adjust length and shape. - Harden folds to maintain shape before simulating again. - Complete sewing on collar parts. ### Butterfly Knot Modeling - Draw two small panels representing the butterfly knot front. - Align the fold angle with the collar’s fold angle. - Copy and arrange symmetrical halves. - Butterfly knot can be sourced from the library with two model types: vpac and trim (secondary key). - For realistic simulation, add the butterfly knot as a clothing document and sew it. - Adjust length and sew with two internal threads front and back, then close the seam. - Simulate to verify butterfly knot realism. ### Additional Embroidery and Threading Details - Coat threads with particles sparingly and add winding lines to collar. - Add two internal threads for roundness. - Fold embroidery parts using the fold tool before sewing.

Add two internal threads for roundness. - Fold embroidery parts using the fold tool before sewing. --- ## Lower Hanfu Components: Kun (Square Panel) and Pants Detailed instructions on creating lower Hanfu components including Kun panels and pants, focusing on scaling, arrangement, seams, and fitting adjustments. ### Kun Panel Creation - Draw a rectangle at 1:1 scale using the internal multi-sided tool. - Use Ctrl key to add curves as needed. - Adjust position using the positioning ball tool. - Classify panels properly as “boards.” - Sew simple seams to connect panels. ### Waist and Pants Adjustments - Add internal lines and folds to waist parts. - Set layer hierarchy to ensure correct layering during wear. - Pants are designed loose with added elastic for fit. --- ## Broken Skirt (Chest and Waist Area) Modeling Focused on designing the complex broken skirt (“broken skirt”) including measurements, panel division, arrangement, sewing, and simulation. ### Measurement and Dimension Setup - Chest circumference: 80.6 cm. - Waist length: 116 cm. - Skirt length: 125 cm. - Total skirt fabric: 6 meters. ### Panel Drawing and Division - Draw a rectangle based on 12-point circle division: - Length: Waist length ÷ 12 = 96.7 cm. - Width: Skirt length ÷ 12 = 125 cm. - Divide rectangle into two T-shapes: 96.7 and 500 units respectively. - Connect and cut to create the T-shaped broken skirt panels. ### Arrangement and Sewing - Duplicate the 12 skirt panels. - Use the positioning ball tool for arrangement around the virtual model. - Sew panels together carefully, adding short points at sewing line endpoints to prevent gaps. - Adjust positions in 2D and 3D windows, ensuring no panel overlap or penetration. - Add fixed pins to prevent skirt fall during simulation. - Harden pins and adjust skirt shape iteratively using pin length and position controls. --- ## Skirt Head and Inner Line Construction Covers creating the skirt head with physical properties and adding inner lines and folds for realistic simulation. - Sew skirt head and add inner lines. - Use folding tools to create fabric folds. - Apply physical element called FiscalRegion for added stiffness. - Set skirt head layer to outermost to ensure visibility. - Adjust skirt shape with fixed pins in simulation mode. - Use pin tools to fine-tune position and angle, preventing skirt falloff. - Increase friction coefficient on skirt to reduce sliding. --- ## Belt Construction and Adjustment Details on creating and simulating the Hanfu skirt belt, including panel drawing, pinning, sewing, and curvature adjustments.

chunks.content: - Use folding tools to create fabric folds. - Apply physical element called FiscalRegion for added stiffness. - Set skirt head layer to outermost to ensure visibility. - Adjust skirt shape with fixed pins in simulation mode. - Use pin tools to fine-tune position and angle, preventing skirt falloff. - Increase friction coefficient on skirt to reduce sliding. --- ## Belt Construction and Adjustment Details on creating and simulating the Hanfu skirt belt, including panel drawing, pinning, sewing, and curvature adjustments. - Draw long and short belt plates using the lifting and folding tools. - Add pins to four sides of plates for positioning. - Adjust curves and folding angles to match garment flow. - Pause during curve drawing to prevent mesh penetration. - Reduce collision thickness gradually to avoid scattering of belt details. - Adjust friction coefficients to reduce sliding effects. - Sew belt panels carefully, adding fixing needles to prevent loop conflicts. - Use fixing needles (W key) to add or delete pins during simulation. - Freeze unrelated panels (clothes, skirts, pants) to improve simulation speed. --- ## Double Eye Knot and Rope Effects Instructions for creating the double eye knot on the knee and simulating rope effects. - Create the knot as either a real knot or a sewing box effect. - Sewing box approach is simpler: create box, adjust shape, place belt over it. - Add fixing needles to secure loose ropes during simulation. - Use positioning ball axes to move knots into desired positions. - Duplicate knots symmetrically as needed. --- ## Fabric Application, Patterning, and Material Adjustment Focus on applying fabrics, adding embroidery patterns, adjusting material properties, and improving clothing quality. - Apply default fabric materials and adjust friction coefficients. - Add embroidery patterns such as group flowers and cherry blossom motifs. - Use texture editing tools to adjust size, direction, transparency, and rotation of patterns. - Lock pattern adjustments before posture changes. - Use posture adjustment tools (combination points) to pose the model. - Adjust transparency during posture changes to balance visibility and quality. - Incrementally improve garment quality by adjusting particle strength, thickness, and stiffness. - Avoid sudden large changes in particle diameter (reduce gradually from 20 to 15 to 10). - Adjust fabric thickness and apply appropriate folds and inner lines. - Use wind control machine to add floating effects to fabric. - Use external software (e.g., Photoshop) for makeup and texture enhancement. - Adjust skin color and material type for realistic skin rendering. --- ## Hair Modeling and Simulation Comprehensive workflow for creating 3D hair using Koro software, panel drawing, texturing, fixing, and simulation. ### Hair Panel Drawing - Use 3D pen model tool to draw hair plates on the scalp. - Use Ctrl key to draw straight lines; delete key to remove errors. - Edit hair shape by increasing curve points. - Cut hair panels flat and apply hair textures. - Duplicate and arrange symmetrical halves. - Adjust thickness and position for realistic appearance.

chunks.content: --- ## Hair Modeling and Simulation Comprehensive workflow for creating 3D hair using Koro software, panel drawing, texturing, fixing, and simulation. ### Hair Panel Drawing - Use 3D pen model tool to draw hair plates on the scalp. - Use Ctrl key to draw straight lines; delete key to remove errors. - Edit hair shape by increasing curve points. - Cut hair panels flat and apply hair textures. - Duplicate and arrange symmetrical halves. - Adjust thickness and position for realistic appearance. ### Fixing Hair on Scalp - Use fixed needle tool to attach hair panels firmly to the scalp. - Adjust shape and eliminate excessive curve points for smoothness. - Add additional fixed needles to secure breakpoints. - Set direct angles and hooks for smoother hair flow. - Apply layering and pressure effects to hair for stability. ### Hair Styling - Convert hole types to “Thunder” for flat effects. - Adjust bottom cast angle and thickness. - Use Edit Curve tool to refine hair shape. - Create curved hair sections with 5 degrees bending. - Arrange hair pieces and fold inner lines for realistic hair strands. - Symmetrize and merge halves, adding internal lines and grooves for shape definition. - Reduce particle diameter for hair to avoid mesh penetration. - Adjust groove angles to prevent tightness and improve movement. --- ## Electronic Hair Bag (Hair Volume Bag) Creation Steps to create a volumizing hair bag using polygon tools and sewing. - Use hexagon tool to create the bag shape. - Adjust powder/responder size for realistic volume. - Increase tape thickness and adjust edge curve settings for smoothness. - Curve rate settings: - 0 for very smooth edges. - 20 for slightly rounded edges. - Wrap electronic hair bag with hair clips. - Sew the bag’s four ends to complete the package. - Convert the bag into a virtual model with negative key to avoid mesh penetration. - Adjust size and position; fix reversed directions. --- ## Additional Hair and Scene Construction Tips - Use fixing needles and stepper pin tools extensively for detailed Hanfu parts. - Adjust hair shape continuously, making it narrower or wider symmetrically. - Define hair color and size appropriately. - Use wind control functions in the 3D window to simulate environmental effects. - Wind control parameters include strength, frequency, and pressure adjustment. - Reduce particle diameter to prevent mesh penetration during simulation.
